brief_summary: Do/don't map. Left column (coral, 'do'): shallow rapid-trigger sensitivity toward Wooting's 0.1mm floor on WASD / rapid re-press keys, plus per-key downstroke/upstroke sliders. Right column (warm-red caution, 'avoid'): the same shallow sensitivity on keys a resting hand touches (left control, thumb keys), with the noise-floor explanation for why tremor/vibration reads as a false double-fire.
data_sources: rapid-trigger-firmware-deep-dive.mdx § 'The tradeoff: an analog signal has a noise floor' — 'Wooting's own setup guidance recommends per-key settings specifically so a board can run aggressive, shallow rapid trigger on the keys that need instant re-press... while leaving keys a resting hand actually touches on a wider, less sensitive setting... The guide names L-Ctrl directly as a candidate for a heavier setting.'
rapid-trigger-firmware-deep-dive.mdx § 'Reset distance is the whole feature' — 'Wooting's documentation states the sensitivity can be set as fine as 0.1mm.'
